en.answer: The astronauts and the ISS are in free fall together. Although Earth's gravity is still strong at orbital altitude (~90% of surface strength), the astronauts, station, and all objects inside are accelerating toward Earth at the same rate due to that gravity. Since everything falls together in orbit, there is no relative acceleration between the astronauts and their surroundings. Weightlessness results from this shared free fall, not from the absence of gravity. An astronaut feels weight only when supported by a surface (a normal force); in orbit, there is no such force.

target.answer: Astronauti a stanica sú v stave voľného pádu. ISS sa pohybuje orbitálnou rýchlosťou (~7,66 km/s) a neustále padá okolo Zeme. Pretože padajú všetci spolu (stanica, astronauti, všetky predmety), ich vzájomný pohyb je bez gravitačného účinku — pociťujú mikrogravitáciu. Nie je to absentcia gravitácie, ale spoločný voľný pád.

en.answer: Metal has much higher thermal conductivity than wood. When you pick up the metal spoon, it rapidly conducts heat away from your hand into the spoon's material, creating a stronger sensation of coldness. The wooden spoon, being a poor conductor, draws heat from your hand much more slowly, so it feels warmer even though both are at the same temperature. The 'coldness' is actually a measure of how fast heat is being extracted from your hand, not the actual temperature of the spoon.
